blocks.source: el león y el ratón, Félix María Samaniego. Estaba un ratoncillo aprisionado. En las garras de un león, el desdichado en la tal ratonera no fue preso por ladrón de tocino ni de queso, sino porque con otros molestaba al león que en su retiro descansaba. Pide perdón, llorando su insolencia.
blocks.translation: The Lion and the Mouse, by Félix María Samaniego. A little mouse was held captive in the claws of a lion. The unfortunate creature had not been caught in this mousetrap for stealing bacon or cheese, but because, along with others, he had disturbed the lion as he rested in his retreat. Weeping over his insolence, he begs for forgiveness.

blocks.source: Al oír implorar la real clemencia, responde el rey en majestuoso tono, no dijera más Tito. Te perdono. Poco después, cazando el león, tropieza en una red oculta en la maleza. Quiere salir, más queda prisionero.
blocks.translation: Hearing the plea for royal mercy, the king replies in a majestic tone—Titus himself could have said no more—"I forgive you." Shortly afterward, while hunting, the lion stumbles into a net hidden in the undergrowth. He tries to escape, but remains trapped.

blocks.source: Atronando la selva, ruge fiero. El libre ratoncillo, que lo siente, corriendo llega, roe diligente los nudos de la red, de tal manera que al fin rompió los grillos de la fiera. Conviene al poderoso para los infelices ser piadoso. Tal vez se puede ver necesitado del auxilio de aquel más desdichado.
blocks.translation: His fierce roars thunder through the forest. The little mouse, now free, hears him and comes running. He diligently gnaws the knots of the net until at last he breaks the beast’s bonds. The powerful should show mercy to the unfortunate: they may one day need help from someone even less fortunate.
